what_this_is: Error categories from four schemes built for languages other than English, read one by one, each with the paper's own words. The inductive half of the language layer: the papers were selected because their title says they define a taxonomy, by a pattern that names no category.
why_it_exists: The deductive half searched for the six properties the Czech scorer already measures. It could confirm them and could not find anything else. These four papers were chosen for being built for a language that inflects or is short of resources, which is the situation the second generation exists for.

elerrant.title: ELERRANT: Automatic Grammatical Error Type Classification for Greek
elerrant.authors: Katerina Korre, Marita Chatzipanagiotou and John Pavlopoulos
elerrant.venue: Recent Advances in Natural Language Processing (RANLP), 2021
elerrant.why_read: A language-specific extension of an English scheme for a language that inflects and carries diacritics. The same shape the second generation needs.

multilingual.title: Multilingual Grammatical Error Annotation: Combining Language-Agnostic Framework with Language-Specific Flexibility
multilingual.authors: Mengyang Qiu, Tran Minh Nguyen, Zihao Huang, Zelong Li, Yang Gu, Qingyu Gao, Siliang Liu and Jungyeul Park
multilingual.venue: Workshop on Innovative Use of NLP for Building Educational Applications (BEA), 2025
multilingual.why_read: It covers Czech, and its structure is a language-agnostic base with language-specific extensions, which is exactly the problem this benchmark has.

repa.title: REPA: Russian Error Types Annotation for Evaluating Text Generation and Judgment Capabilities
repa.venue: Workshop on Balto-Slavic Natural Language Processing (BSNLP), 2025
repa.why_read: Ten error types that humans annotated on generated text in an inflected Slavic language, and a measurement of how a judge does in it rather than in English.

talktag.title: TalkTag: Fine-Grained Morphosyntactic Error Annotation for Transcribed Speech
talktag.why_read: Clinical morphosyntactic annotation of transcribed speech: the setting of the Czech track, where the transcript is speech recognition output.

what_this_changes_for_the_six: Three of the six now have a named category in a published scheme rather than a count of papers that mention the word: diacritics has Greek ACC, agreement has Greek VERB:SVA and the Czech application of the multilingual framework, and the untranslated term has Russian Code-Switching. Calque, register and non-word do not, from these four papers.
what_nobody_here_had_thought_of: UNK - an error that can be detected but not corrected

the_judgement_is_the_assistants: What each category means for this catalog is written next to the words it was read from, and nothing is added to the catalog here.
still_unread: Thirteen of the seventeen fetched papers and 47 of the 64 in the frame. Seventeen of the 21 that name a language in the title are unread.

categories.quote: ACC Accentuation Accentuation addition or removal.
categories.what_it_means_here: The first published support for the Czech scorer's diacritics criterion, and it arrives in the shape that matters: not as prose about how accents are hard, but as one error type of fourteen in a working classifier for a language that has them. Greek is not Czech, and an accent in Greek marks stress where a Czech diacritic can change the word, so the rule transfers and its severity does not.

categories.quote: VERB:SVA Subject Verb Agreement The subject and the verb to be in person agreement.
categories.what_it_means_here: Agreement as its own error type rather than a corner of grammar. The Czech scorer bundles agreement, case and an unfinished sentence into one criterion; this paper separates them, which is the direction to take rather than a disagreement.

categories.quote: WO Words Order Error in words order.
categories.what_it_means_here: Nobody on this project proposed word order, and it is a category in both schemes built for an inflected language. In Czech word order carries emphasis and given/new structure rather than grammatical role, so a note can be grammatical and still say the wrong thing by its order. None of the 36 candidates asks about it.

categories.category: UNK - an error that can be detected but not corrected
categories.quote: UNK Unknown error type An error that can be detected but not corrected.
categories.what_it_means_here: A category for being able to see that something is wrong without being able to say what the right version is. This project has the same instinct written as a rule -- an absence is never a measurement -- and no category that implements it for a language error. Worth having, because the alternative is a rater silently choosing between a wrong label and no label.

categories.category: the language-agnostic base: Missing, Replacement, Unnecessary, crossed with part of speech
categories.quote: Our approach combines a language-agnostic foundation with structured language-specific extensions, enabling both consistency and flexibility across languages.
categories.what_it_means_here: The structural answer to the question the second generation asks. An error is missing, replaced or unnecessary, crossed with the part of speech it touches; that much holds in any language, and what each language adds sits on top and is declared. This is the shape the Czech criteria should have had from the start, instead of six flat properties with no relation to the English ones.

categories.category: Czech word order annotated with the part of speech involved
categories.quote: For Czech, the example highlights differences in word order (WO) annotation: our method distinguishes between auxiliary and main verbs by incorporating POS information, whereas prior work generally treated such cases as generic WO errors.
categories.what_it_means_here: Czech is one of the five languages the framework was actually applied to, against a published Czech error corpus. So there is a Czech reference point for this, which is more than the catalog had for any of the six.

categories.quote: Code -Switching: The chatbot 's response contains unexpected switching between languages.
categories.what_it_means_here: Support for the untranslated-term criterion, from a Slavic language, as one of ten error types that human annotators actually labelled. The paper's definition is wider than ours -- any unexpected switch, not only a technical term left in English -- which is an argument for widening ours rather than for keeping it narrow.

categories.category: Fluency, defined by whether comprehension is hindered
categories.quote: Fluency: The response contains critical grammatical errors that may hinder text comprehension.
categories.what_it_means_here: The useful part is the threshold. Not every grammatical slip counts, only one that may stop a reader understanding. The catalog's language criterion has no such threshold, so it treats a missing comma and an unreadable sentence as the same kind of finding.

categories.quote: Sudden Interruption: The chatbot 's response was abruptly cut off.
categories.what_it_means_here: This project treats a cut-off answer as a harness failure: finish_reason decides whether a row is usable, and a truncated note never reaches scoring. REPA treats it as a property of the text that a human rates. Both can be right, and which one this benchmark wants is a decision nobody has made.

categories.category: a judge does worse in Russian than in English
categories.quote: Our findings reveal a notable gap between LLM judge performance in Russian and English.
categories.what_it_means_here: Not a criterion, a warning. This benchmark judges Czech notes with judges whose calibration was measured on English, and the one paper that measured the same thing for a Slavic language found the judge worse there. The calibration against the two human annotators has to be repeated in Czech, not carried over.

categories.category: flagging the cases automated tagging cannot decide
categories.quote: effectively identifying instances where linguistic ambiguity makes automated tagging genuinely complex
categories.what_it_means_here: The same idea as the Greek UNK category, and from a clinical setting with transcribed speech, which is this track's setting exactly. A tool that says which cases it could not decide is the tool this project's own rule asks for.
